properties.title: NIC proposed network — data-driven placement (towns x hazard), loadout per site
properties.note: COMPUTED placement, every marker a real town (GeoNames) or a real arc site — no lattice. Rules: stations go where people can build and maintain them; countries with dense existing networks (JP/TW/US/NZ/IT/CH/CL/MX/GR/IS) get only major hubs; backbone fills empty ~800 km cells with the biggest town in the cell. Each marker carries its LOADOUT (populate for the place, not full-kit: no snow radar in the tropics, cosmic-ray heads only at high latitude, air-quality only in real cities) and its UNITS (a big city on a fault gets extra nodes for EEW aperture — +1 per ~1M people, cap 6). Coastal arrays follow the DIRECTIONAL RULE: the 50-year source map is the known trenches, so each site is a 5-sonde fan on the source-facing sector only (4 where DART watches the deep leg upstream); the lee shore is wave shadow and gets nothing; an island reachable from TWO arcs keeps the ring (8 sondes); cabled seas (S-net/DONET, NEPTUNE, GeoNet) keep only interop hubs. The radar sea-gauge goes only where a real town (<= ~100 km) can host and keep the mast — a bare exposed shore drowns or de-masts a surface gauge, so elsewhere the slope-toe magnetometer is the gauge. Each coastal marker carries its CABLE-KM (shore -> slope toe, per-arc budget) and TOE-DEPTH-KM; where a real islet sits seaward on the slope the station snaps to it by name (islet-first: the mainland haul collapses to ~10-30 km). Totals: 2,086 seismic towns (2,237 nodes) + 168 coastal arrays (796 sondes, 15 of the sites hubs on cabled seas, 6 multi-threat rings, radar at 51) + 194 backbone = 2,448 sites, ~3,227 deployed units. Orange=seismic (belt towns) · red=coastal array · grey=backbone (geomag/TEC).
properties.sources: GeoNames via all-the-cities (pop>=20k) · priority-tsunami/earthquake.geojson · existing-systems.geojson (DART) · GAIA.md
